name: canvas-crowd

frames.best_why: A full band of black-and-white hand-drawn people fills the lower stage with varied faces and postures.

tagline: Hand-drawn black-and-white characters stroll back and forth across the bottom.
summary: A canvas strip of sketchy black-and-white people walking across the bottom of the screen. Characters enter from both sides at different depths and leave, so the crowd keeps cycling, with a small label centred above.
appearance: A stark black background with a thick horizontal band of black-and-white line-drawn figures along the bottom edge. The people differ in hats, hair and posture, drawn at several depths so heads overlap, and a tiny grey label sits at the top centre.
behaviour: Each figure walks across the strip at its own pace with a slight bob, then leaves and respawns from the opposite side or another depth. The crowd keeps cycling so the band stays full.
demo_content: A tiny label reading "Join 40,000 makers" over an illustrated character sheet.
search_phrases: people walking across bottom of screen
use_when: A community or launch page wants a lively human crowd as decoration without photos.
avoid_when: It loads a remote sprite sheet from an external bucket and draws continuously, which costs battery.
customise: Props set the sprite sheet URL and the small label; the rows and columns, walk speed and crowd density are fixed in the source.
weight_why: Paints up to 105 sprite figures to a canvas every frame from the GSAP ticker.

a11y.note: The canvas is decorative and silent, and the endless walk ignores reduced-motion, so it keeps moving for users who ask it not to.

issues: The crowd relies on a remote sprite sheet that fails offline.
The top label is tiny, faint and easy to miss.
polish_why: Charming, coherent illustration and a lively crowd; the label is almost illegible.
title: Canvas Crowd
